new_value:
• Magadha (Statement 4) is directly associated with the Buddha: he attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, preached at Rajgriha, and received royal patronage from King Bimbisara and King Ajatashatru.
• Kosala (Statement 3) is directly associated with the Buddha: he spent 21 rainy seasons (vassa) at the Jetavana monastery in Sravasti, Kosala's capital, under King Prasenajit's patronage.
• Avanti (Statement 1) is incorrect: although its ruler King Chanda Pradyota invited the Buddha, the Buddha did not visit in person; instead, he sent his disciple Mahakaccana to preach Dhamma there.
• Gandhara (Statement 2) is incorrect: located in the far northwest (modern Pakistan and Afghanistan), the Buddha never visited it during his lifetime; Buddhism spread there much later under Emperor Ashoka and the Kushans.
• Often confused with: Gandhara's prominence in Buddhist art (Greco-Buddhist / Gandhara school) and Avanti's later Buddhist centers (like Sanchi in Vidisha), which leads candidates to mistakenly assume the Buddha personally visited them.
issues_found: Original explanations often fail to clarify the distinction between areas where Buddhism flourished later (Avanti and Gandhara) versus regions the historical Buddha actually visited and lived in during his lifetime (Kosala and Magadha).
